title: A task added to a running phase can be worked
description: A task added to a phase that is already running is born `pending`, and the plan gate resolves allowed paths through `in_progress` tasks only - so its own declared files are refused on the first edit. Field report 12 measured two executors returning zero edits and spending their tokens on a refusal that names the wrong cause. There is no CLI verb that promotes a task without also spawning one, so the only route is an orchestrator Edit of the shard.
desiredOutcome: A task added to a running phase can be worked without a hand edit of the shard: one verb promotes it, under the same lock and journal row every other mutating verb carries, and refuses a terminal task. And when the plan gate does refuse, its message names which of the two causes it is - the file is not in any task's files, or a task declares it and is not started - because a message that misdirects costs a round trip that a message that refuses does not.

tasks.title: audit-task.py start: the verb that promotes a task without spawning one
tasks.description: `audit-task.py` gains a `start <taskId>` verb: it writes `status: in_progress`, `startedAt` and `attempts += 1` - exactly the three fields `reference/orchestrator.md` already prescribes an orchestrator Edit for - under the index lock, with a journal row, revalidating the manifest afterwards like every other mutating verb. It refuses a `done` or `cancelled` task, and says so. Widening `_config.in_progress_task_map` to read `pending` was considered and rejected: it has three consumers and would open every file declared by every pending task in the running phase, deleting the per-task narrowing the decision order exists for.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: start promotes a pending task and journals it; a done or cancelled task is refused by name

tasks.title: The plan gate's refusal names the cause it actually found
tasks.description: `require-plan.py`'s refusal names which of the two causes it is. Today a path that IS in a task's `files` and in `fileIndex`, whose task is merely `pending`, draws "Outside the running plan" and - on the subagent branch - "report that <path> is outside your task's `files`", which the manifest contradicts. The gate holds the fact and discards it: `in_progress_task_map` filters the task out before the decision is made. Carry the distinction into the message: the file is in no task's files, or a task declares it and is not started, with the remedy for each.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_require_plan.py: a path declared by a pending task draws a refusal naming the status, not the scope
